channel.title: Hoops Intel — Daily NBA Scores & Analysis
channel.description: Your daily NBA intelligence briefing with scores, player rankings, injury reports, and game previews.

item.title: Wagner Scores 38, Brooklyn Hangs 145, Luka and Wembanyama Each Score 32
item.description: Zion scores 29 in the loss; Porter and Demin each score 22; Murray has 30 and Jokic 27-11-8 — Franz Wagner scored 38 points and 8 rebounds in Orlando's 123-108 win at Utah, the high score on Wednesday's ten-game slate. Brooklyn won 145-111 at New Orleans with Zion Williamson scoring 29 and Michael Porter Jr. and Egor Demin each scoring 22. Luka Doncic scored 32 and Victor Wembanyama scored 32 with 5 blocks.

item.title: Celtics Dismantle Sixers on the Road, Portland Stuns OKC, and the East's Hierarchy Gets Its Clearest Reshuffling of the Young Season
item.description: Boston's 123-101 road demolition of Philadelphia hands BOS sole possession of the East's best record at 10-2 while Scoot Henderson's 34-11-6 masterclass powers Portland's stunning 20-point upset of Oklahoma City — Scoot Henderson delivered the night's most complete individual performance — 34 points, 11 assists, 6 rebounds, and 3 steals — as the Trail Blazers stunned the Thunder 123-103 at Moda Center, while Jayson Tatum's 31-9-7 road orchestration dismantled Philadelphia 123-101 on NBC to hand Boston sole possession of the East's best record at 10-2 and New York's 32-point demolition of Milwaukee confirmed the Bucks' 1-10 organizational crisis is no longer an early-season anomaly

item.title: Spurs Blow Out Phoenix 122-96, Warriors Demolish Pelicans 138-87, Lakers Stay Hot at 10-2
item.description: Castle's 32-9-5 leads San Antonio's 26-point road demolition; Golden State posts season-widest 51-point margin; LeBron closes back-to-back road win at Atlanta — Stephon Castle delivered 32 points, 9 assists, 5 rebounds, and 3 steals as San Antonio dismantled a Durant-less Phoenix squad 122-96 on the road, lifting the Spurs to 9-2 and cementing their status as the West's most dangerous road team alongside Golden State's 138-87 annihilation of New Orleans — the NBA's widest margin of the 2026-27 season — and LeBron James's 29-10-8 closing performance in a 124-114 back-to-back road win at Atlanta that kept Los Angeles atop the West at 10-2.

item.title: Lakers Win in Detroit to Stay at 9-2, Celtics Rout Milwaukee 117-97, Sixers Lead East at 9-2
item.description: LeBron's 31-9-7 closes out a road win at Detroit as LAL maintains West co-leadership; Embiid's 36-11-5 on a probable tag cements Philadelphia atop the East; Harden's 38-point explosion shocks New Orleans in LA's season-high 139-point output — Joel Embiid returned from a knee-soreness probable tag to deliver 36 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 blocks in Philadelphia's 127-121 road survival at Chicago, lifting the Sixers to 9-2 and cementing their position atop the Eastern Conference alongside Boston's 8-2 professional dismantling of a Milwaukee team that has now collapsed to 1-9.

item.title: Spurs Romp Portland 125-103, OKC Blitzes Washington 114-75, Three West Teams Share 8-2 Record
item.description: Booker's 38-Point Stunner Topples 7-3 Houston Without Durant; Castle's Back-to-Back Road Dominance Settles ROY Race; Knicks Win in Cleveland as East Tightens — Devin Booker scored 38 points on four three-pointers to lift Phoenix past Houston 102-99 without Kevin Durant in the young season's most surprising upset, while San Antonio's 22-point road demolition of Portland and OKC's 39-point blowout of Washington left three Western Conference teams tied at 8-2 after ten games.

item.title: Thunder Dismantle Grizzlies by 31, Lakers Hold Off Portland, and the West's Hierarchy Snaps Into Focus on a Nine-Game Friday
item.description: Oklahoma City's 31-point road demolition of Memphis moves the Thunder to 7-2 as the West's new standard; LeBron's fourth-quarter authority closes out Portland; Spurs, Celtics, and 76ers all make statements on a loaded Friday slate — Oklahoma City's 128-97 destruction of Memphis at FedExForum was the NBA season's most authoritative team performance to date — a 31-point road win against a 6-2 Grizzlies team that the desk had projected as a one-possession game. SGA's 34-8-6 anchored the blowout and OKC climbs to 7-2 as the West's new first-tier standard.

item.title: Warriors Dismantle Heat 120-100, Suns Rebound Past Magic 117-104
item.description: Golden State climbs to 6-3 behind Curry's 29-point statement on NBA TV while Booker carries Phoenix without Durant; nine-game Friday slate led by Lakers hosting Trail Blazers — Golden State's 20-point dismantling of Miami on NBA TV was the Warriors' most complete performance of the season, with Stephen Curry's 29 points and Draymond Green's triple-double neutralizing a Butler-led Heat team depleted by back-to-back West Coast travel. Phoenix collected a necessary bounce-back win over Orlando behind Devin Booker's 32-point, 7-assist performance without Kevin Durant, dropping the Magic to 2-6 and raising organizational questions about their early-season identity.

item.title: Philadelphia and Portland Lead the Way After a 14-Game Wednesday: 76ers Win in Detroit, Blazers Stun the Suns, and Two Overtime Games Close the Night
item.description: PHI Stays Hot at 8-1, POR Blazes to 7-1 · OKC and SAS Both 6-2 After Big Wins · OT Thrillers in New Orleans and LA Close a 14-Game Slate — Portland's 132-119 demolition of Phoenix — the desk's identified trap game all week — pushed the Blazers to 7-1 behind Scoot Henderson's 31-point, 11-assist road showcase, while Philadelphia's 112-106 win at Detroit confirmed the 76ers as the East's undisputed best team at 8-1. The night closed with back-to-back overtime finishes: Miami stunned the Clippers 117-116 on Butler's clutch free throws, and New Orleans edged Utah 120-113 behind Zion's 30-10-6.

item.title: PHI and HOU Share NBA's Best Record at 7-1 Ahead of Loaded 14-Game Wednesday Slate
item.description: Zion Williamson's OT game-winner ends Memphis's perfect season; PHI-DET and SAS-DAL headline Wednesday's ESPN doubleheader — Zion Williamson hit a go-ahead overtime basket at Memphis to end the Grizzlies' perfect season and lift New Orleans to 4-3, while Philadelphia and Houston both reached 7-1 on Monday's 15-game slate. Wednesday's 14-game card is headlined by a PHI-DET collision on ESPN that represents the East's first genuine hierarchy test of the young season.

item.title: New Orleans Ends Memphis's Perfect Season in OT, Detroit Keeps Rolling, and the NBA's Standings Shake Up on a 15-Game Monday Slate
item.description: Williamson's 34-point overtime masterpiece stuns the Grizzlies 135-134 at FedExForum, Sengun posts 31-14 as Houston routes Boston to reach 7-1, and LeBron drops 29-11 in a 138-117 Lakers rout of Miami — Zion Williamson scored 34 points including a go-ahead basket with 38 seconds left in overtime to give New Orleans a stunning 135-134 road win over Memphis, ending the Grizzlies' perfect 6-0 start and delivering the night's most narratively significant result on a loaded 15-game slate.

item.title: Boston Rolls Orlando 108-97 to Stay Hot at 5-1, Lakers Edge Toronto 131-125 in High-Scoring Thriller, Warriors Beat Clippers 124-112 as Curry Stays Scorching
item.description: LeBron's 14-point fourth quarter rescues bounce-back home win, Curry posts 77 points across two nights, and Brooklyn stuns Indiana on the road as the Nets find proof of concept — LeBron James overcame a nine-point third-quarter deficit with a 14-point fourth quarter to deliver a 131-125 home win over Toronto at crypto.com Arena, moving the Lakers to 5-2 and completing the bounce-back narrative entering Sunday's slate.

item.title: Memphis Stays Perfect at 6-0 With 31-Point Demolition of Sacramento, Cleveland Erupts for 136 in Milwaukee, Portland Rolls to 22-Point Road Win in Utah
item.description: Grizzlies are the NBA's last unbeaten team; Bucks fall to 1-5 after surrendering 136 at home; Trail Blazers' 4-1 start is the West's most underrated story — Memphis improved to 6-0 with a 136-105 dismantling of Sacramento, making the Grizzlies the NBA's last remaining unbeaten team while the Kings dropped to 0-6 as the league's lone winless squad

item.title: Miami Drops 145 in Halloween Offensive Explosion · Detroit Stays Hot at 5-1 With Road Win in Brooklyn · Denver Edges Phoenix to Move to 3-2
item.description: Curry drops 41 with seven threes to end Lakers' five-game streak, Jokic posts 33-14-9 road masterpiece in Phoenix, and Butler anchors season-high 145-point Heat explosion on Halloween night — Stephen Curry scored 41 points and hit seven three-pointers — the most by any player in a single game this season — to end the Los Angeles Lakers' five-game winning streak at Chase Center in a dominant Golden State performance on Halloween night

item.title: Memphis Remains the West's Last Unbeaten Team After Dismantling Portland, Atlanta Shocks Cleveland in Overtime Thriller, and New Orleans Ends Sacramento's Winless Start
item.description: Grizzlies reach 5-0 with 21-point road win at Moda Center as Ja Morant posts 29-11-6, Trae Young's 31-13 closing performance stuns the Cavaliers 114-111 at State Farm Arena, and CJ McCollum's 34-point six-three explosion lifts the Pelicans past 0-5 Sacramento — Memphis's 124-103 road demolition of Portland — holding Scoot Henderson to 14 points on 5-of-17 shooting while outscoring Portland's bench by 19 — makes the Grizzlies the NBA's sole remaining unbeaten team at 5-0 and the West's most credible organizational story heading into November

item.title: Houston Steamrolls Milwaukee to Reach 5-0 While Lakers Dominate Clippers and Dallas Stuns OKC
item.description: Rockets blew out Bucks 132-100 to remain NBA's last unbeaten team, Lakers cruised past Clippers 103-87 in LA rivalry opener, and Mavericks ended Thunder's perfect start with a 120-96 demolition — Houston's 132-100 road demolition of Milwaukee at Fiserv Forum certified the Rockets as the NBA's last perfect team at 5-0, with Alperen Sengun posting 31 points, 14 rebounds, 6 assists, and 3 blocks against Giannis Antetokounmpo in the night's most dominant individual and organizational performance

item.title: Portland Shocks the Lakers in LA While Boston Survives a Nets Overtime Scare and San Antonio Announces Itself With a 27-Point Blowout of Sacramento
item.description: The Trail Blazers stunned Los Angeles 136-129 to move to 3-0, the Celtics needed overtime to beat Brooklyn 125-124 to reach 3-1, and the Spurs demolished Sacramento 130-103 at Frost Bank Center in the night's most dominant team performance. — Portland's 136-129 road victory in Los Angeles is the night's most organizationally disruptive result — the Trail Blazers are the West's only unbeaten team after passing their toughest test emphatically at crypto.com Arena against a Lakers squad widely projected as a top-three Western Conference seed.

item.title: Memphis Goes 4-0, OKC Stays Perfect, Golden State Stuns Denver on the Road
item.description: Curry drops 38 in a 20-point road blowout, Mitchell rallies Cleveland past Minnesota in overtime, and four West teams remain unbeaten after a nine-game slate — Stephen Curry erupted for 38 points and six three-pointers as Golden State stunned Denver 134-114 on the road, delivering the night's most shocking result and reversing the Warriors' 1-3 narrative in a single performance, while Memphis reached 4-0 with a road win at Utah and Oklahoma City stayed perfect behind SGA's 33-point showing against Kevin Durant

item.title: Indiana Announces Itself as a Legitimate Eastern Conference Force While Detroit Delivers the Night's Most Organizationally Significant Upset
item.description: The Pacers dismantled Brooklyn by 27 on the road, Detroit stunned Philadelphia to hand the 76ers their first loss, and the Lakers moved to 3-0 with a comfortable Salt Lake City win. — Detroit's 106-93 road win in Philadelphia handed the 76ers their first loss of the season as Cade Cunningham orchestrated a defensive masterpiece with 27 points, 9 assists, and 3 steals, moving the Pistons to a surprising 3-0 start and forcing a full recalibration of the East's early power structure.

item.title: Houston Announces Itself as a Genuine Western Conference Power While Washington and San Antonio Deliver the Night's Biggest Upsets
item.description: Rockets move to 3-0 with road win over Atlanta, Spurs stun Dallas by 16 as 7-point underdogs, and Jokic posts 38-15-9 in overtime thriller — Houston's 121-114 road win over a 2-0 Atlanta team confirms the Rockets as the West's most complete team through three games, while San Antonio's 16-point road demolition of Dallas as a 7-point underdog stands as the night's most stunning result and Milwaukee's 0-3 start has reached organizational emergency designation.

item.title: Atlanta and Detroit Announce Themselves as Early-Season Contenders While Portland Keeps Stunning the League
item.description: Hawks demolish Charlotte by 47 points, Pistons cruise in Miami, and Trail Blazers go 2-0 with another road stunner in Sacramento — Atlanta's 128-81 demolition of Charlotte — the largest margin of the young season — combined with Detroit's comfortable road win in Miami and Portland's second straight road statement to define the NBA's most consequential early-season night, with Scoot Henderson's 34-point, 10-assist masterpiece headlining a slate that reshuffled the league's power-structure conversation in both conferences

item.title: Philadelphia Stays Perfect · OKC Suffocates Denver · West's Top Seeds Look Ruthless Through Two Nights
item.description: The 76ers rolled past Cleveland 114-106 to move to 2-0. Oklahoma City held Denver to 84 points in a 96-84 defensive clinic. Two nights in, the West's ascending teams look capable of something special and the East's pecking order is already shifting. — Oklahoma City's 96-84 defensive clinic over Denver held Nikola Jokic and the Nuggets to 84 points in their season opener, while Philadelphia moved to 2-0 with a professional 114-106 execution over Cleveland, establishing OKC and PHI as the West and East's most complete teams through two nights of play.

item.title: Night Two Delivers a Power Statement: West's Best Look Ruthless, East's Surprises Pile Up
item.description: Minnesota demolishes Miami by 25, Portland obliterates Phoenix by 41, Lakers open 1-0 over Golden State on ESPN, while Washington, Atlanta, and Indiana add East upsets — Portland's 124-83 annihilation of Phoenix and Minnesota's 131-106 road demolition of Miami headlined an eleven-game slate that exposed Milwaukee and the Suns as organizational concerns while confirming the Lakers, Timberwolves, and Blazers as legitimate West forces through two days of play

item.title: Detroit Stuns Boston on Opening Night · Philly Silences MSG · OKC Answers the Bell in San Antonio
item.description: SGA erases a 1-4 preseason with a 38-point road demolition of San Antonio, Cunningham leads the Pistons past the preseason's only unbeaten team, and Maxey carries Philadelphia to a stunning road win at Madison Square Garden. — Oklahoma City silenced every preseason doubter with a 116-104 road win over San Antonio as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander delivered 38 points on 15-of-24 shooting, flipping OKC's entire organizational narrative in a single opening-night performance.

item.title: Opening Night 2026-27: Boston at Detroit Headlines Three-Game Slate as Regular Season Begins
item.description: Celtics enter 4-0 after dominant preseason; Pistons host as East's reigning top seed; OKC must answer 1-4 preseason record at Wembanyama's Frost Bank Center — The 2026-27 NBA regular season tips off with three games — BOS at DET, PHI at NYK, and OKC at SAS — with Boston entering as the preseason's only unbeaten team and Oklahoma City carrying the league's most alarming preseason record at 1-4 into San Antonio.

item.title: Preseason Closes With No Games — Boston Enters Opening Night 4-0, Sacramento Enters 0-5
item.description: Sunday's total off-day seals every preseason organizational verdict as permanent; the 2026-27 NBA regular season begins October 20 — Boston finishes the preseason as the only unbeaten team in the league at 4-0, headlined by a road overtime win at Philadelphia, while Sacramento's 0-5 disaster carries directly into the regular season with no corrective window remaining.

item.title: Boston Locks In at 4-0 as Preseason's Last Unbeaten; Sacramento's 0-5 Disaster Enters Opening Week
item.description: Friday's off-day freezes every organizational verdict — Celtics hold the window's most credible East confirmation while Kings absorb another 24 hours of the preseason's most damaging narrative with no corrective opportunity — Boston's 4-0 preseason record, sealed by a road overtime win at Philadelphia on October 17, stands unchallenged as the window's most credible East organizational confirmation after an off-day locks it as the definitive baseline entering the final weekend before opening night October 20.

item.title: Boston Goes 4-0 with OT Win at Philly, Atlanta Demolishes Dallas by 24, Sacramento Falls to 0-5
item.description: The Celtics survived overtime at Philadelphia to remain the preseason's only unbeaten team, the Hawks road-demolished Luka's Mavericks to surge to 4-1, and the Kings completed the window's most alarming organizational collapse entering opening night — Boston's 125-120 overtime road win at Philadelphia gave the Celtics a 4-0 record — the preseason's only unbeaten mark — while Atlanta's 24-point demolition of Dallas at American Airlines Center confirmed the Hawks as the East's most surprising ascending story and Sacramento's fifth straight loss sealed the window's most complete organizational disaster

item.title: Knicks Edge Raptors in OT Thriller, Rockets Blow Out Thunder by 27 on NBA TV
item.description: New York survives 122-120 at MSG to end 0-4 nightmare; Houston's national-TV demolition of OKC drops SGA to window's loudest established-star alarm at 1-4 entering 12-game Friday finale — Houston's 116-89 demolition of Oklahoma City on NBA TV is the preseason window's most damaging single-night result for an established West star, dropping OKC to 1-4 and rendering Tuesday's corrective win over Indiana contextually hollow. Alperen Sengun's two-way Toyota Center showcase is the window's most complete emerging-center confirmation on national television.

item.title: Detroit Stuns Minnesota by 22, Chicago Rolls Milwaukee by 21, Pelicans Escape Dallas in Final Seconds
item.description: Seven-game Wednesday slate reshuffles the preseason power map as Milwaukee collapses to 1-3, New Orleans rises to 3-1, and Boston remains perfect at 3-0 entering opening week — Detroit's 128-106 road demolition of Minnesota at Target Center is the night's most alarming result for an established West contender, dropping the Timberwolves to 3-2 while the Pistons rise to 2-1, as Chicago's 125-104 road blowout at Fiserv Forum drops Milwaukee to 1-3 and registers as the desk's loudest East established-star alarm entering opening night

item.title: Toronto Drops 148 on the Knicks, Orlando Rolls Cleveland, and OKC Finally Wins in Overtime as the Preseason Hits Its Final Week
item.description: Tuesday's five-game slate produced a 50-point demolition at Scotiabank Arena, a 16-point Kia Center statement, an OT thriller at Paycom Center, and Golden State handing the Lakers an ugly loss at T-Mobile Arena as opening night pressure mounts. — Toronto's 148-98 destruction of New York at Scotiabank Arena is the preseason window's most alarming single result — a 50-point margin that leaves the Knicks at 0-4 and exposes a structural system-identity crisis six days before opening night.
